newsitem.title: UK: Cardiff to host single currency summit.
newsitem.headline: Cardiff to host single currency summit.

text.p: Britain said on Tuesday it had chosen Cardiff, the capital of Wales, to host the European Union summit in June 1998 which is to decide which countries qualify for the first wave joining the single European currency.
Prime Minister John Major announced the decision on the venue in a written answer to a parliamentary question.

"The European Council will be held in Cardiff," he said. The summit will come at the end of Britain's six-month presidency of the EU, and just six months before the single currency is due to be launched on January 1, 1999.

If this date is adhered to, the summit will have to decide which countries have qualified to join by their economic performance and leaders of those countries will have to say whether they will sign up for the project.
Britain's Chief Secretary to the Treasury, William Waldegrave, said on Tuesday the chances of Britain joining the single currency in 1999 were decreasing with every day that passed.
"As each day goes by...it is increasingly unlikely that Britain will be there at the start," he told a financial industry awards ceremony.

The last time Britain held the EU presidency, in 1994, it chose Edinburgh, the Scottish capital, as the venue for the summit. Major is a strong supporter of the "union", the name given to the four constituent parts of Britain.
